name: University of Wroclaw
summary: Wroclaw university operating since 1702, with 12 faculties; 12 English-taught bachelor's, from Biotechnology to an environmental-law LLB.

ib.text: IB holders skip the foreigners' entrance exam on every bachelor's except Biotechnology. The IB Diploma counts as B2 English and needs no recognition in Poland.

lastYear.text: apply 2 February–31 August; Biotechnology by 24 July

programmes.name: Biotechnology
programmes.about: Lab-heavy biotechnology: molecular biology and genetic engineering, cell culture and bioinformatics, with electives and internships aimed at pharmaceutical, medical and environmental biotech.
programmes.overview: You study cell structure and organelles, biomolecules such as sugars, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids, the transmission of genetic information, human physiology and the immune system, metabolic pathways, bioinformatics, and biotechnology applied to pharmaceuticals and agriculture. A large share of your time is spent in the laboratory running experiments, analysing results and writing reports, with internships and electives that let you steer towards your career interests. Graduates work as research scientists, industrial, medical or agricultural biotechnologists, project managers, lab technicians, clinical medical representatives, science editors and teachers, or start their own ventures.
programmes.ib: Every foreign applicant, IB holders included, sits an online oral exam in biology and chemistry (pass mark 10 of 20).
programmes.selectionNote: Oral exam in biology and chemistry, 0-20 points, at least 10 to pass; places go to passing candidates within the limit (30 in 2026). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: Business and Administration
programmes.about: Leadership, marketing, accounting, finance, management, international economics and law in a common two-year core, then a third-year specialisation in Business, Finance or Governance.
programmes.overview: The curriculum covers leadership, marketing, accountancy, finance, management, research methods, international economics, entrepreneurship, law, human resource management and intercultural communication. Years one and two follow a common curriculum, and in year three you choose a specialisation in Business, Finance or Governance. Graduates are prepared to manage in multinational firms, work in consulting and marketing, start a business, advise on investment and finance, or run a non-profit.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 170 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: Chemistry
programmes.about: General chemistry through lectures and lab classes: modern methods of chemical synthesis and physico-chemical techniques for studying the structure of compounds.
programmes.overview: The programme teaches general chemistry with an emphasis on modern methods, including chemical synthesis, physico-chemical methods for studying the structure of compounds, and physical and chemical measurement techniques. Lectures are combined with laboratory classes on modern equipment. Graduates can work in laboratories, in companies that use modern technologies, in research institutions and diagnostic laboratories, in industry and at universities.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 24 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: Criminal Justice
programmes.about: Substantive criminal law, criminal procedure, criminology and forensic science, aimed at careers in policing, the courts, prisons and probation, and public or private security.
programmes.overview: You study substantive criminal law, criminal procedure, criminology and forensic science, with a focus on preventing and countering crime in its social and economic context and on international aspects of criminal justice. Graduates are prepared for public security institutions such as the police and penitentiary services, support roles in the judiciary, government and local administration, private security firms, and international organisations and EU institutions.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 150 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: Culture, Thought and Humanity
programmes.about: Philosophy applied to culture: how ideas shape cultures and how they can support dialogue between them, with a focus on contemporary crises and humanity's place on the planet.
programmes.overview: The programme looks at culture through philosophy: philosophy of culture, social and political thought, cultural and philosophical anthropology, cultural psychology and sociology of culture, including concepts of the person between nature and culture and the practice of cultural criticism. It has international links, including with a centre in the United States, and teachers from different parts of the world. Graduates can work in NGOs promoting intercultural dialogue, humanitarian and refugee organisations, media, cultural institutions and PR, as critics, journalists, cultural managers or political analysts, and can continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 30 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: Data and Society
programmes.about: Sociology for a data-driven world: how data is produced, read and used in work, cities, migration and digital life, with research workshops where you design studies and analyse real datasets.
programmes.overview: Classical sociology meets analytical skills: labour studies, urban sociology, migration studies, digital cultures, big data analytics, research methodology, critical theories of technology, coding basics, statistical modelling, qualitative research and data visualisation. Learning is by doing, in research workshops, analysing real datasets and designing your own studies, with training in presenting findings to policymakers, NGOs, social movements and companies. Graduates are prepared for work in policy analysis, data and research consultancy, urban development, migration and integration services, digital innovation, public administration, NGOs and international bodies, or for a master's in the social sciences.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 50 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: English for Knowledge, Culture and Innovation
programmes.about: Advanced English skills with linguistics and literature; from year two you choose Global English Cultures and Languages or Psycho-Pedagogical Aspects of Language Acquisition.
programmes.overview: You develop practical English (grammar, speaking, reading, writing and pronunciation), study linguistics and English and American literature, and learn Polish plus one more language from scratch: German, French, Spanish, Italian or Russian. In the second year you choose between Global English Cultures and Languages, on varieties of English, pragmatics and intercultural communication, and Psycho-Pedagogical Aspects of Language Acquisition, on language learning, processing and the psychology of acquisition. Experimental methods in the study of language and the mind feature in the course. Graduates have data analysis, linguistic and cultural skills, and the programme prepares for CELTA and DELTA teaching qualifications and for master's study in linguistics, literature, culture or education.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 50 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: European Cultures
programmes.about: Europe's cultural heritage through archaeology, art history, cultural studies, history and social psychology, with most courses chosen by the student.
programmes.overview: Lectures and seminars draw on ancient archaeology, cultural studies, art history, the history of Poland and Europe, social psychology and cultural and classical pedagogy, looking at communication systems, symbolic structures, cultural and political history, how values are transferred and European cultural heritage. Few courses are obligatory and most are elective, so you shape your own programme. The aim is to train people who can translate between cultural codes and organise cooperation between European societies, working in HR and PR for multinational firms, public administration, cultural institutions, tourism and journalism.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 20 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: Genetics and Experimental Biology
programmes.about: Biology at the cellular and molecular level, with small-group lab work in genetic engineering, histology, cytology and physiology; a new programme.
programmes.overview: The curriculum covers cell structure, metabolism and division, nucleic acids and the genetic code, inheritance, genetic engineering techniques such as DNA electrophoresis and PCR, virology, microbiology, plant and animal diversity, and ecology. Laboratory sessions are held in small groups with specialised equipment and modern techniques in genetic engineering, histology, cytology and physiology, with some classes online. Graduates work in pharmaceutical and food laboratories, police forensic laboratories, environmental protection, plant and animal breeding, and research institutions, or continue to a master's in natural sciences.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 20 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: International Relations - Global Studies
programmes.about: Globalisation studied as a process in its own right, linking local and global events; the programme includes four semesters of Polish and one of another foreign language.
programmes.overview: Globalisation is studied as an autonomous process shaping all national and international actors, through economics, international relations, political science, anthropology, sociology, area studies and cultural and ethnic studies, with some input from earth sciences and physics. The course mixes obligatory courses, specialty courses and optional seminars, plus Polish language, a second foreign language and physical education, and ends with a bachelor's thesis under a professor's supervision or a bachelor's examination. International student exchange is possible.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 50 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: International and European Environmental Law
programmes.about: Law on the protection and use of the environment, from human rights to sustainable development, alongside the basic disciplines of law, for work in international bodies and environmental organisations.
programmes.overview: The programme gives a legal education centred on the protection and use of the environment, covering all the basic legal disciplines and treating international environmental problems holistically, including human rights and sustainable development. It aims to train specialists and entrepreneurs in environmental law. Graduates may work in international and European organisations, environmental departments of companies, specialist environmental firms and institutions, NGOs for nature protection, or as self-employed professionals.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 150 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

programmes.name: Political Science
programmes.about: Political theory, institutions, campaigns and media analysis, with a third-year specialisation in Media and Politics, Comparative Politics, Global Security or Europe in the World.
programmes.overview: The course covers political doctrines and institutions, contemporary political processes, politics and the media, political marketing and research methods, policy analysis, media content analysis, public speaking and strategic communication. Teaching includes international exchanges and research projects involving government institutions, media organisations and international companies, alongside international students and practitioners. In year three you choose Media and Politics, Comparative Politics, Global Security or Europe in the World. Graduates work as political advisers, campaign managers and policy consultants, in news, PR and political communication, in government, think tanks and international organisations, or in political consulting and public affairs firms.
programmes.selectionNote: No ranking for IB holders: B2 English and a positive review by the course coordinator; offers roll within 40 places (2026 limit). 2027 rules.

notes: EU citizens pay a lower EU rate than non-EU students, e.g. €2,400 a year against €3,900 for Business and Administration (2026/27).
Everyone without Polish citizenship, EU citizens included, applies through the international registration; Polish citizens use a separate system.
An offer becomes a place only once the first year's fee is paid, within 4 weeks of the offer.
